q: Plants lack a nervous system like animals. (2026-Set 2)
e: Plants do not have a nervous system; instead, they coordinate responses using plant hormones.

q: Internal stimuli or internal control are chemicals called plant hormones. (2025-Set 9) (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Plant hormones act as internal chemical regulators to control growth and responses.

q: Plants can respond to their environment in various ways. (2024-နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: Plants respond to environmental stimuli such as light, gravity, touch, and moisture.

q: Growth in general is considered as an increase in size of the object. (2025-Set 2)
e: Growth generally involves a permanent increase in size, dry mass, or volume.

q: Meristematic phase occurs in shoot apex and root apex. (2025-Set 4)
e: Active cell division during the meristematic phase occurs in the shoot and root apices.

q: Growth can be defined as an irreversible increase in size of an individual cell or organ or its parts. (2025-Set 12)
e: Biological growth is an irreversible process leading to a permanent increase in size.

q: Growth regulators are manufactured by dead protoplasm. (2024-Set 2)
e: Growth regulators are manufactured by living protoplasm.

q: Genetic factors are not involved in overall maintenance of a plant. (2024-Set 3)
e: Genetic factors play a crucial role in controlling growth and overall maintenance of a plant.

q: All parts of seed plants produce cytokinin. (2026-Set 1)
e: Cytokinins are primarily synthesized in actively dividing tissues like root tips.

q: Auxins are strong organic acids produced naturally by plants. (2025-Set 1)
e: Auxins are weak organic acids naturally synthesized by plants.

q: Auxin, gibberellin and cytokinin are growth inhibitors for plants. (2025-Set 11)
e: Auxins, gibberellins, and cytokinins act as plant growth promoters.

q: A plant hormone is an inorganic compound. (2024-ရန်ကုန်နှင့်တိုင်းခရိုင်အချို့တွင်မေး)
e: A plant hormone is an organic compound that regulates physiological processes.

q: In hypogeal germination, the cotyledons are first pushed above the ground by the rapid elongation of hypocotyl. (2026- နိုင်ငံခြား)
e: In epigeal germination, cotyledons are pushed above ground, whereas in hypogeal germination, they remain below ground.

q: Hypogeal germination takes place above the ground. (2024-Set 4)
e: Hypogeal germination takes place below the ground surface.

q: Soybean is short night plant. (2025-Set 3)
e: Soybean is a short-day plant, which requires long uninterrupted dark periods (long night).

q: Effect or requirements of relative length of day and night on flowering is called photoperiodism. (2024-နောက်ဆက်တွဲမေးခွန်း / 2025-Set 8)
e: Photoperiodism refers to the response of plants to the relative duration of light and dark periods.

q: A stimulus is detected by a sensory receptor. (2025-Set 5)
e: Sensory receptors specialized cells or structures that detect changes in the environment.

q: Reflex arcs are simple connections of only two neurones to transmit messages.(2025-Set 7)
e: Most reflex arcs involve three types of neurones: sensory, interneurone (relay), and motor neurone.

q: Motorneurones are found entirely within the central nervous system. (2026- Set 2)
e: Interneurones are located entirely within the central nervous system, while motor neurones extend into the peripheral nervous system.

q: Neurones are the basic structural and functional units of the nervous system.(2025 Set 9)
e: Neurones are the core structural and functional nerve cells of the nervous system.

q: Individual neurones are organized into tissues called glial cells. (2025-Set 13)
e: Glial cells are non-neuronal support cells in the nervous system, not tissues composed of neurones.

q: The endocrine glands and their hormones make up the nervous system. (2025-Set 10)
e: Endocrine glands and hormones form the endocrine system, not the nervous system.

q: Endocrine glands secrete chemical messengers called hormones. (2025-Set 6)
e: Endocrine glands release hormones directly into the bloodstream to serve as chemical messengers.
